scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

F-01.statement: Route completion for manual meter reads was 0.88 against a 0.95 target over 2026-08..09, covering 9200 manual-read accounts.

F-02.statement: CRM dispute tickets (2440 total): median response 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, against a 3.0-day SLA.

F-03.statement: Disputed bills by read type: 1240 ESTIMATED, 1785 ACTUAL (billing-db breakdown).

F-04.statement: Billing-db tariff change log shows 0 records, i.e. no tariff change was logged in the relevant period.

F-05.statement: CRM monthly dispute ticket volume: 610 (2026-06), 590 (2026-07), 1180 (2026-08), 1260 (2026-09) — roughly doubling from June/July baseline to August/September.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 permits the utility to request route priority changes but requires execution to be confirmed by the Field Operations Manager.

F-07.statement: route-log lagging_routes query returned 14 records with distinct completion values per route; sample record shows route R-00 at 0.70 completion.

F-08.statement: 320 accounts received an estimated bill in the last cycle, spanning 40 distinct routes (billing-db accounts_estimated_last_cycle).

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

H-RESPONSE-HANDLING-GAP.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a response-handling/throughput problem (slow or templated replies), and an auto-answering agent on CRM tickets is the right fix, including for whatever causes wrong bills.

H-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August altered acceptance/estimate-substitution logic, causing incorrect bills and the resulting dispute surge.

H-AMI-EXPORT-DEGRADATION.statement: The nightly AMI/MDMS export to billing (H-MDMS-BILL) degraded in delivery or semantic validity since August, pushing more accounts to estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-DEGRADATION.statement: The manual meter-read handoff from Field Services (H-FIELD-BILL) degraded in delivery or validity since August (e.g. incomplete routes, invalid reads), driving more estimated/wrong bills.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: A field staffing shortfall at the contractor reduced route completion rates since August, independent of handoff mechanics, causing missed reads and bill errors.

H-TARIFF-IMPORT-ERROR.statement: A billing import/validation or tariff-application error affects bills regardless of read type (including ACTUAL reads), explaining the majority of disputed bills not attributable to estimate substitution.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The field route-completion log shows manual-read routes achieved only 0.88 completion against a 0.95 target for 9200 accounts in Aug-Sep 2026, indicating a real shortfall in manual meter-read coverage during the dispute-surge period.
CRM data shows median dispute-ticket response time is 1.6 days and p90 is 2.8 days, both inside the 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets, i.e. response speed/throughput is not failing against SLA.

Of disputed bills broken down by read type, 1785 had an ACTUAL meter read and 1240 had an ESTIMATED read, so a majority (59%) of disputes occur on bills that were NOT estimate-substituted. This means read-collection/export degradation (AMI or field) can at most explain the ESTIMATED-read minority of disputes, leaving the larger ACTUAL-read dispute population unexplained by those mechanisms.

The billing-db tariff change log returned zero records, meaning no tariff rate/structure change was logged in the system of record for the relevant period, so a tariff-change event cannot explain the dispute surge or wrong bills.

CRM monthly dispute counts rose from ~600/month in June-July 2026 to ~1180-1260/month in August-September, quantifying the stakeholder's 'doubled since August' claim as a real, roughly 2x volume increase with an August onset; it only confirms the surge's existence and timing, it does not identify which causal mechanism (read collection, import rules, response handling) drives it.

E-06.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL, a stakeholder (non-authoritative), claims there has been no tariff change this year, which agrees in direction with the already-authoritative billing-db tariff change log (E-04, zero records). This is a corroborating claim, not new authoritative evidence, and does not identify any new causal mechanism for the dispute surge or wrong bills.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD claims a three-reader staffing shortfall since July causes routes to run late, pushing affected customers onto estimated bills — a specific causal story for the already-observed 0.88 route completion rate (F-01), but it remains an uncorroborated stakeholder claim from a source with a disclosed incentive (contract headcount increase) and bias (attributes problems to staffing).

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract (E-08) establishes that while the utility may request route priority changes, execution requires confirmation by the Field Operations Manager (SH-FIELD) — this is the documentary basis for the existing K-DISPATCH human-approval requirement on push_route_update, not new information about the dispute-surge cause.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: The route-log lagging_routes query returns 14 specific routes with distinct completion values (sample: route R-00 at 0.70 completion), decomposing the aggregate 0.88 completion rate (E-01) into per-route detail; it confirms route-level shortfall granularity but does not by itself identify why these 14 routes lag (staffing vs. other factors).

E-10.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: The billing-db accounts_estimated_last_cycle query (E-10) shows 320 accounts received an estimated bill in the last cycle, spread across 40 distinct routes. That distinct-route count (40) exceeds the 14 lagging routes previously identified in E-09, so the field route-completion shortfall (the lagging 14 routes) can at most account for a fraction of the routes producing estimated bills; the comparison is caveated because "last cycle" scope/timing versus the Aug-Sep dispute window is not stated.
